description:
Advances: ancora.gate

The re-entry option recorded in ancora.decision.no_execution_no_state has been triggered: the M9 Atlas perf acceptance (ancora-yzu.25) missed all five budgets on the fleet's largest corpus (216 subjects, 2,086 requirements) — median-of-3 warm: spec.check 37,213ms vs 10,000 budget; spec.prime 31,860 / spec.next 19,984 / spec.status 16,862 / spec.validate 10,348 vs 5,000 each. Manuel ruled merge-now-cache-fast-follow on 2026-09-03: Atlas ships on ancora 1.0 carrying the honest latency, and this ticket owns closing the gap.

Shape per the founding ADR: an on-disk cache keyed by git object id, so unchanged blobs skip repeated parse/AST work across invocations. Constraints the design must keep: the cache is LOCAL, UNCOMMITTED state (gitignored, disposable, rebuildable from scratch) — nothing like specled_ex's committed baselines, whose drift classes the no_execution_no_state charter exists to prevent; a cold or corrupted cache must degrade to today's behavior, never to a wrong answer; and the decision's Negative paragraph should be amended (with clause accounting if requirement prose changes) when this lands. Acceptance: re-run the Atlas bench (bench/gate_bench.exs, median-of-3, warm build) on the Atlas corpus and land spec.check under 10s and the report tasks under 5s, or return to Manuel with the honest residual. Sibling fast-follow: ancora-n24 (retirement vocabulary) — a 1.0.x/1.1 release can carry both; hex publish is operator-only (Manuel's 2FA).

Sequencing: blocked by ancora-xla.3. That ticket removes the in-memory waste (unnarrowed base tree, per-binding MapSet rebuild, re-parse) which no blob cache touches. Re-run bench/gate_bench.exs on the Atlas corpus after xla.3 merges and record the residual on this ticket before designing the cache; if the residual already clears the budgets, return to Manuel with the numbers instead of building the cache.

Ruling needed before code moves (Manuel): after the xla.3 re-measure, is an on-disk OID cache still worth reopening ancora.decision.no_execution_no_state?
Recommended default from the ticket: build it only if spec.check on the Atlas corpus is still over 10s warm after xla.3. If built: gitignored local state, keyed by git object id, a cold or corrupt cache degrades to today's behavior, and the ADR's Negative paragraph is amended in the same diff.
Worker: if no comment on this ticket records a ruling when you start, park and ask. Do not choose on Manuel's behalf and do not implement more than one option.

Verification:
- Tests to pass: tagged tests under ancora.gate and ancora.derive for the cache path (test/ancora/gate_test.exs, test/ancora/derive/**, test/ancora/git_test.exs); a property that the verdict and finding set are identical with cache absent, warm, and deliberately corrupted
- Behaviors to demonstrate: (1) identical spec.check output on the same repo with no cache, a warm cache, and a truncated cache file; (2) the cache directory is listed in the scaffold .gitignore guidance and never appears in git status of a consumer; (3) median-of-3 warm bench on the Atlas corpus: spec.check under 10,000ms and each report task under 5,000ms, numbers posted on this ticket, or the honest residual posted and the ticket returned to Manuel
- Verification cadence:
  - Iteration tier: mix test --stale or explicitly named test files, plus mix spec.validate; no full suite mid-iteration.
  - Final tier: immediately before IMPLEMENTED, run-until-green: mix compile --warnings-as-errors && mix test && mix format --check-formatted && mix deps.unlock --check-unused && mix spec.check --base the epic base sha recorded at admission
  - Verifier tier: mix spec.check --base the epic base sha recorded at admission plus tagged and --stale selections only; do NOT run the full suite.
- Standing bounce-class checks:
  - Production call site named for each new callable surface, with the proving test that exercises that production path.
  - Fixture hygiene: one TmpGitRepo per test, no shared temp dirs, async only where the fixture allows.
  - Spec surfaces kept fresh for every touched callable surface. Drift, growth, and shrink clear only through substantive requirement or scenario edits in the same diff, never through a Spec-Ack trailer.
  - Every conditional clause covered by a test.
- proves: the gate gives the same answer with a cold, warm, or corrupted cache, and the Atlas corpus clears its budgets or the residual is on record.

Allowed touches (this ticket may modify):
- lib/ancora/git.ex, lib/ancora/git/**
- lib/ancora/derive.ex, lib/ancora/derive/run_context.ex, lib/ancora/derive/extract.ex, lib/ancora/derive/def_index.ex
- lib/ancora/base_view.ex, lib/ancora/gate.ex, lib/ancora/config.ex (a cache location or off switch only)
- a new lib/ancora/cache.ex or lib/ancora/git/oid_cache.ex
- bench/**
- test/ancora/**
- .spec/specs/ancora.gate.spec.md, .spec/specs/ancora.derive.spec.md (substantive requirement for cache-transparent verdicts)
- .spec/decisions/ancora.decision.no_execution_no_state.md (amend the Negative paragraph; clause accounting if requirement prose changes)
- priv/spec_init/** and docs/migration.md, README.md (gitignore guidance and the off switch)

Out of Scope (files):
- lib/ancora/review/**
- lib/ancora/parser.ex
- lib/ancora/verifier.ex
- lib/mix/tasks/** beyond threading one option

Out of Scope (intent):
- no committed state of any kind; nothing resembling specled_ex baselines
- no wrong answer on a stale cache: a miss or mismatch always recomputes
- no re-doing xla.3's in-memory fixes here

Merge gate:
- [ ] mix compile --warnings-as-errors
- [ ] mix test
- [ ] mix format --check-formatted
- [ ] mix deps.unlock --check-unused
- [ ] mix spec.check --base the epic base sha recorded at admission ends result=pass
- [ ] Scope check: diff touches only Allowed globs (mechanical)
- [ ] Auditor APPROVE comment on the ticket

comments.text: RULING (Manuel, 2026-09-03): deferred out of ancora-xla. Ancora was split from specled_ex to carry less state and less PR churn, and an on-disk cache is exactly the kind of second source of truth the no_execution_no_state charter exists to keep out. ancora-xla.3 (narrowed base tree, hoisted path set, parse once per side) is expected to remove most of the measured Atlas time; nobody has benched Atlas after those fixes. This ticket reopens only if a post-xla.3 median-of-3 warm bench on the Atlas corpus still puts spec.check over 10,000ms, and the founding ADR's re-entry clause is the only door. If the numbers come back merely over budget rather than far over, the first argument is a budget change, not a cache. Still blocked by ancora-xla.3 so the dependency is visible. Revisit date set to 2026-10-01 as a reminder, not a commitment.

Bench-condition update from the ancora-gg8 investigation (2026-09-03, findings-DE on that epic): the phase decomposition shows xla.3's fixes live entirely in the gate path — after xla.3 alone, spec.validate is untouched, status/next/prime barely move, and check likely lands mid-20s, so four of five budgets would still be missed and the deferral bench would be measuring the wrong residual. The 2026-10-01 revisit bench should run after ancora-xla.3 AND the gg8 perf tickets (ancora-gg8.4 waste fixes, ancora-gg8.7 parallel parsing). The deferral ruling itself stands: merely-over-budget argues a budget change, not a cache. Also recorded there: the blocked-by edge to xla.3 is measurement sequencing, not a technical dependency.

title: On-disk OID cache for gate performance (Atlas re-entry)
